characteristics.cultivar: Qi Lan (related to Anxi cultivars, adapted to Wuyishan)

description.short: Aromatic rock oolong featuring a pronounced floral ('orchid') bouquet grounded in Wuyi's signature minerality
description.overview: Originally hailing from southern Fujian (Pinghe / Anxi), this cultivar was brought to Wuyishan where it acclimated to the rocky volcanic soil, retaining its brilliant floral fragrance while absorbing the deep mineral character of northern Fujian rock tea.
description.leaf: Dark brown, medium-twisted leaves with roasted sheen
description.aroma: Pronounced floral orchid bouquet intertwined with light mineral notes
description.taste: Floral, subtly sweet, supported by the mineral foundation typical of Wuyi terroirs
description.processing: Standard Wuyi rock tea methodology, crafted with a slightly gentler charcoal roast to preserve delicate floral volatiles

history.origin: The name translates to 'Rare Orchid' (or 'Mystic Orchid'), directly reflecting its unmistakable orchid-like aroma.
history.development: Originally bred in southern Fujian, its adaptability led to its introduction into Wuyishan as a favored variety both for single-cultivar production and aromatic blending.
history.modern: Today, Wuyi Qi Lan is prized for its exquisite balance between southern Fujian floral brightness and northern Fujian cliffside minerality.
interestingFacts: Because of its intense floral projection, Qi Lan is sometimes mistaken for Guangdong Dancong oolongs, despite hailing from entirely different botanical lineages and terroirs.
Cultivating the Qi Lan cultivar across different Fujian regions (Anxi, Pinghe, and Wuyishan) offers a masterclass in how terroir shapes the final character of identical genetics.
